subject: design-technology
title: Typography
welcome_lead: Fonts, hierarchy and choosing letters that work.
final_note: Text is design too — pick fonts on purpose.

concepts.def: Font with tiny strokes at ends.
Order of importance shown by size.

walkthroughs.body_html: Serif fonts (Times New Roman) have tiny strokes at letter ends — feels traditional, used in books. Sans serif (Helvetica, Arial) is clean and modern — used on signs and screens.
Hierarchy shows what to read first. Big bold heading, medium subheading, small body text. Without it, the reader doesn't know where to look.
Kerning tightens or loosens space between letters. Leading (pronounced 'ledding') is the gap between lines. Good spacing makes text readable.
